display_rule: A source dependency is an exposure pathway, not a forecast of failure. Annual mixes must be refreshed when a utility supplies a dated report.

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: City retail supply is approximately 97–99 percent surface water and roughly 2 percent groundwater in the cited profile; surface portfolios include Salt/Verde and Colorado River sources.
primary_exposures: Colorado River allocation and operating rules
growth pressure in the larger Phoenix Active Management Area
cities_and_regions.critical_qualification: The Phoenix AMA groundwater model is not a finding that the City of Phoenix utility runs out of water.

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: Approximately 90 percent Colorado River water from Lake Mead and 10 percent local groundwater.
primary_exposures: Lake Mead intake and water-quality operations

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: Water is delivered through wells, including recovered Colorado River water previously recharged into the aquifer; physical delivery is therefore not equivalent to exclusively native groundwater.
primary_exposures: groundwater quality and local well conditions

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: 2024 mix: 44 percent Rio Grande, 36 percent Hueco Bolson, and 20 percent Mesilla Bolson; brackish-groundwater desalination supplements the portfolio.
primary_exposures: Rio Grande drought and interstate/international allocation
energy and concentrate management for desalination

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: San Juan–Chama surface water and the Santa Fe Group aquifer are operated as a joint portfolio.
2025 deliveries: 44 percent Los Angeles Aqueduct, 52 percent Metropolitan Water District imports, 1 percent local groundwater, and 3 percent recycled water.
primary_exposures: Eastern Sierra hydrology and environmental constraints
Colorado River and State Water Project reliability

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: Portfolio includes Colorado River transfers, Northern California imports, local supplies, recycling, and the 50 Mgal/d Carlsbad seawater desalination plant.
primary_exposures: drought and wildfire impacts on local sources

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: Surface reservoirs and connected rivers supply the system; Dallas does not use groundwater as a source.
Planning profile is approximately 86 percent surface water and 14 percent groundwater.
Edwards Aquifer supplied approximately 47 percent in 2025, with other aquifers, surface water, reuse, and desalinated brackish water providing diversification.
primary_exposures: Edwards Aquifer recharge and drought pumping restrictions

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: The highly permeable Biscayne aquifer is the primary drinking-water source.
cities_and_regions.critical_qualification: The cited county model found no wellfield impact through 2040 under its evaluated high sea-level-rise case; this is not a guarantee after 2040 or under every operational condition.

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: Approximately 2.8 million people depend on about 400 Mgal/d pumped through roughly 1,500 wells in a sole-source aquifer system.
primary_exposures: coastal flooding of wells and treatment assets
cities_and_regions.critical_qualification: Localized intrusion can close or relocate wells even when the regional freshwater volume remains large.

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: Floridan aquifer groundwater serves the region; a chloride plume is documented in part of the aquifer system.
Potomac River water treated by the Washington Aqueduct is the current source.
cities_and_regions.adaptation_context: Pure Water DC is being developed as a resilience/source-diversification strategy.

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: Mississippi River water is treated for drinking supply.
cities_and_regions.critical_qualification: The 2023 salt wedge was episodic and did not reach city intakes during the posted event; it is not evidence of permanent source loss on a fixed date.

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: An upstate reservoir and aqueduct system supplies approximately 1 Bgal/d to more than 9 million people.
Portfolio blends groundwater, river water, off-stream storage, and a 25 Mgal/d seawater desalination plant.
cities_and_regions.adaptation_context: Regional planning evaluates additional capacity in 2033 and 2043 horizons.

cities_and_regions.supply_profile: Surface-water-dependent regional system under current Stage 3 drought restrictions at the access date.
cities_and_regions.critical_qualification: Restriction level and reservoir percentage are volatile status fields and must be automatically refreshed.
